change: Combine flat-list text-run DOM shape/text validation and ownership-map validation in one run iteration, removing the duplicate shape/text traversal. The separate wrapper-map ownership walk remains. Every block, run, wrapper, attribute, child count, text value, identity, placeholder and map count check remains mandatory. No validation cache or skipped subtree; base paragraph validation retains its existing path. No Rust, wire, public API or declaration change.
tests: 162 renderer cases passed against the unchanged runtime, including 13 new before-observer drift cases covering block/wrapper attributes, wrapper tag/children/comments/nesting, text value/identity, extra runs and placeholder shape/count.
After the runtime edit, all 1857 browser tests across 52 files and strict source/test TypeScript passed.
Five full DOM/controller/composition/clipboard/toolbar/queue/history/native IndexedDB V6 autosave/recovery runs passed in each of Chromium, Firefox and WebKit.
Private packed consumers passed in all three engines; base Node, strict TypeScript and Chromium smoke passed using the same installed packages. Shipping trees were verified unchanged.
toolingFailure: The initial renderer test command ran Vitest from the repository root instead of the browser workspace and lacked jsdom: 159 failures reported document is not defined, with 3 passing. Correcting the command to npm test --workspace @breditor/browser -- src/dom_renderer.test.ts yielded the 162-case unchanged-runtime baseline. This was a test-environment error, not a runtime regression.
reproduction: node scripts/measure-flat-list-performance.mjs <package-record> (alternate the baseline and candidate records twice)

BREDITOR_FLAT_LIST_BINDINGS=target/flat-list-candidate-Rq6C5V BREDITOR_LIST_TEST_PORT=4193 PLAYWRIGHT_JSON_OUTPUT_NAME=target/list-single-pass-demo-20261004.json npx playwright test -c playwright.lists.config.ts --reporter=line,json --output target/list-single-pass-demo-20261004
measurementMethod: Sequential old/new/old/new using unchanged production minified installed-package full-editor fixture; no concurrent Breditor build/test. Reports are relative to the corresponding consumer. Each run passed all 27 correctness cases (three repetitions at 10/100/500 items per engine), 108 total. No diagnostic instrumentation or JIT changes. Background host load was not controlled; values are rounded to one decimal millisecond.
interpretation: All engine medians improved in both local pairs, but this is not statistical or universal latency evidence. Second-pair WebKit ranges overlap. Firefox 500-item edits still take about 191-193 ms and remain an open responsiveness concern. These clean runs do not establish the cause or fix of historical WebKit faults.
nativeQualification: No new physical-keyboard IME or spoken VoiceOver evidence. The human checklist on port 4194 and older native preview on port 4188 remain bound to their earlier artifacts, not this optimized browser package.
